page.layout: One page of text, one full-width column. Page number 238 at the top left, running head DESCRIPTIO at the top centre. No margin notes. Faint marks at the right edge and lower left are show-through or the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: mero& viribus imparem in fugam egit. Fugientium plurimi omissa Corintho recta Arcadiam petiere cum duce Dizeo: qui si Corinthum se recepissent, & ad urbis ejus defensionem vel modicè animos obsirmassent, sine dubio reliquam victoriam difficiliorem Mummio fecissent, & melioribus deditionis conditionibus urbem reservassent. Mummius vero Corinthum ducens turpiter ab Achaeis defertam, & à maximo quoque civium numero relictam, cum ad eam devenisset, quamvis apertas portas reperiret, tamen metu latentium insidiarum ingredi eam aufus non fuit. Tertio demum die, exploratis jam omnibus, impetu violento eandem invasit, occupatamque, ut in mandatis habebat, diripuit, incendit, vastavit, funditus excidit, excisamque sine habitatore reliquit. Manubiæ omnes ditissimæ & clarissimæ urbis Romam devectæ: viri in urbe reperti in primo furore statim occisi, fœminæ cum pueris sub corona venditi. Post hunc gravissimum Corinthi casum reliquæ urbes omnes belli hujus participes Mummio litæ[?], ab eoque munitionibus nudatæ, arma viris adempta: omnia hæc primè confecta priusquam adessent[?] Romam venturi, quorum con-silio

page.notes: The word "adessent" is partly obscured where the line ends; the final "nt" is hard to read and the reading is marked [?]. "litæ" after "Mummio" is doubtful, and the colon before it may be a printing error. "nudatæ" is partly lost at the line end. The last word is "con-" with "silio" at the start of the next line, printed with a long s that looks like f; it is read as silio. Faint marks at the right edge and lower left are show-through from the reverse side and are omitted. Original spelling is kept, including "vinditi" and "devectæ".
